name: Martin Krutský
affiliation: Intelligent Data Analysis Lab, FEE, Czech Technical University in Prague
tagline: Mechanistic interpretability · Neurosymbolic AI · Responsible AI
about: I am a PhD student at the Intelligent Data Analysis Lab, Faculty of Electrical Engineering at the Czech Technical University in Prague, supervised by Gustav Šír. My research is on neurosymbolic mechanistic interpretability: logic-guided circuit discovery, sparse feature learning, and provably sufficient explanations of graph neural networks. Previously, I worked on symmetry-invariant deep learning and binarized GNNs for combinatorial optimization.

This autumn, I am an Applied Research Intern at Superhuman (formerly Grammarly), using natural language autoencoders to explain AI-text detectors and AI humanizer models. I am also part of the EleutherAI Summer of Open AI Research (SOAR), studying sparse autoencoder pathologies that mimic feature hierarchy.

I co-founded Responsible AI in Prague, an initiative organizing talks, debates, and the Prague Workshop on Responsible AI. Our research assesses explainability methods for AI governance. I also bring 5+ years of industry ML engineering, from NLP models to shipped LLM applications.
